extracted.intended_audience: securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations (FINRA), securities legal practitioners, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_short: SEC rule filing and withdrawal notice
extracted.subtask_description: Official Federal Register notice describing the filing, publication, suspension/proceeding, comment receipt, extension, and withdrawal of a proposed rule change under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Focused on procedural steps for SRO rule filings and Commission disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing authority for proposed rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule changes must be filed with the Commission pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "On January 2, 2024, Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. ('FINRA') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission ... pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, proposed rule changes..." (includes statutory citation: 15 U.S.C.78s(b)(1); 17 CFR 240.19b-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness upon filing for fee/due changes (Section 19(b)(3)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change may take effect upon filing with the Commission if it is designated by the exchange as 'establishing or changing a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the self-regulatory organization on any person, whether or not the person is a member of the self-regulatory organization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text cites 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(A) and 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(A)(ii) and notes: 'The proposed rule changes were immediately effective upon filing with the Commission pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Federal Register and Commission action
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule changes are published in the Federal Register; the Commission may temporarily suspend the proposal and institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'On February 13, 2024, the proposed rule changes were published in the Federal Register and the Commission temporarily suspended and instituted proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule changes.' (references Securities Exchange Act Release Nos. and FR citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and record of public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission receives and records public comments on proposed rule changes; comments are cited and summarized in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'The Commission received six comments on the proposed rule changes and one response to those comments.' The notice lists the senders and dates of comment letters (e.g., letters from industry participants and plan representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of extended review period under Section 19(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may designate a longer period within which to approve or disapprove proposed rule changes under Section 19(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'On July 31, 2024, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act, the Commission designated a longer period within which to approve the proposed rule changes or disapprove the proposed rule changes.' Example: designation of October 10, 2024 as the date for Commission action (see cited Release Nos.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of proposed rule changes by filer
rubrics_metrics.description: A filer (here, FINRA) may withdraw proposed rule changes; the Commission issues a notice acknowledging the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'On September 5, 2024, FINRA withdrew the proposed rule changes (FINRA-2024-002; SR-FINRA-2024-003).' The notice records the withdrawal date and file numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document heading and metadata requirements for Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents include headings and metadata such as agency name, docket/file numbers, release numbers, FR citation, document number, publication date, page numbers, and may identify CFR titles/parts and RINs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text (Document Headings section): headings 'may contain the following: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN...' and refers users to the Document Drafting Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official-format and legal-status verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The FederalRegister.gov XML rendition is a prototype and not the official legal edition; users should verify against the official PDF on govinfo.gov because only official editions provide legal notice and judicial notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'This site displays a prototype... It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register... Each document posted on this site includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov.' Also: 'Those relying on it for legal research should verify their results against an official edition of the Federal Register.' Cites 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507 regarding legal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegated signature and authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices may be executed 'for the Commission' by a Division official pursuant to delegated authority, with delegation authority cited in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.' Footnote cites 17 CFR 200.30-3(a)(12). The notice shows the Assistant Secretary's name and that delegated authority is documented.
